title: World Games
build: Epyx disk, 1986, two sides (C64 Preservation Project G64s, world_games_s1[epyx_1986](pal) and world_games_s2[epyx_1986](pal), MD5 2ab5a751... and f983b43d...)

records.c: weightlifting's entry, from the shell. RAM everywhere but the I/O ($01 = $35), the SID's voice 3 set to noise at its highest frequency and 256 readings of it ($D41B) kept at $0400-$04FF as random numbers ($197D); zero page $10-$FF cleared, colour RAM from $3C00, the music's frequency table built ($2806), dark grey background, a multicolour bitmap at $6000 with its colours at $5C00 in VIC bank 1, all eight sprites on, the raster interrupt at line 160 through the vector at $FFFE ($1781). The lift starts with the snatch ($EF = 2) at 75 kilograms ($37 = 15, the weight in steps of 5 kg), and every player's score is cleared
the shell's unpacker reads the packed file's header here ($1000-$1004) while it unpacks; once it is done, weightlifting's start-up
the packed file's header, its third byte, read by the shell's unpacker before the event's bytes replace it; here, the operand of LDX #$FF
the packed file's header, its fourth byte, read by the shell's unpacker; here, the TXS
the last byte of the packed file's header the shell's unpacker reads; here, the LDA of $35

a new event, or another practice: first attempt ($39 = 1), first player, the three text rows cleared, the lifter's standing pose (script 0, its first frame only, $3A = $80), the opening tune (13), the plates for the weight ($1985). In a competition "PRESS THE BUTTON TO START."; in practice "PRACTICE WHICH EVENT?" with SNATCH or CLEAN AND JERK beside it, up for the snatch and down for the clean and jerk; the fire button goes on ($1188)
the shell's unpacker reads the packed file's last header offset here before the event's own bytes replace it; here, the operand of LDX #$00

the music stopped; then each lifter's turn: the player's record (32 bytes, $47 the player) copied to $0500 and its name and country printed in text row 1, the judges' six lamps grey, "SNATCH #n" or "CLEAN AND JERK #n" in row 0 ($1631), the standing pose, the weight chosen ($13B7), "BEGIN LIFT." and the lift's script (2 for the snatch, 3 for the clean and jerk) run to its end. A lift that ends overhead (result $3D = 1) goes to the judges ($14ED); any other gets three red lamps

after the lift: in practice, the question of another; in a competition, with two white lamps or more, the weight becomes the player's best at this lift ($16 of the record for the snatch, $17 for the clean and jerk) and the lowest weight for the rest ($37)

the next player; after the last, the next attempt: the round's lowest weight goes up 5 kg if anyone lifted, "PRESS THE BUTTON TO CONTINUE.", and after three attempts the clean and jerk from 75 kg again, or after its three the end ($12DF)

waits for the fire button; before a lift's first attempt the attempt's title blinks, 32 frames on and 32 off. Then waits until the lifter's joystick is known ($53) and its fire button is let go, redraws the plates and goes to the next lifter

the end of the event: after the fire button, each player's score is the snatch and the clean and jerk added ($14B2, times 5 kg): its text, three digits (a space for no hundreds), a space and "KG" at $10-$15 of the record, its value as one digit a byte, units at $16, tens at $17, hundreds at $18. Then $55 tells the interrupt to end the event, and this waits for it
waits for the interrupt at line 0 to end the event ($17C7)
in practice, after a lift: "PRACTICE AGAIN?" with YES or NO, which up and down change; the fire button on YES starts again ($10F4), on NO ends the event

the choice of weight: "PLEASE SELECT THE WEIGHT." and "CURRENT WEIGHT" with the weight in kilograms, which right raises (to 225 kg, $2D) and left lowers (not below the round's lowest, $37), a step for each push, repeating every 8 frames once held for 32; each step plays tune 2 and redraws the plates. The fire button ends it, and the weight's timing factor from $1493 goes to $4B
the shell's unpacker's copy loop has $1400 as a placeholder operand; here, the operand of ORA #$30, the weight's hundreds digit
the joystick's left and right, against the reading of the frame before ($36)

for each weight from 75 to 225 kg, the timing factor: the good part of each of the lift's timing windows, out of 256 ($FF at 75 kg down to 1 at 225 kg, where only the window's last frame is good); the heavier the weight, the later and shorter the moment to push
A times 5, in kilograms, as a number in binary-coded decimal in $1E-$1F: the product's bits added up from the table of powers of two at $1615

the judges, for a lift held overhead: the lifter's skin changes colour the longer the hold ($1572, every 64 frames); the judges vote one at a time ($1577), the first after $45 frames and each of the others up to 31 frames after the one before, white while the hold is under 48 frames, red after. Down on the joystick puts the weight down ($1536); held for 255 frames, the lift ends badly ($1546)
the weight put down: the judges who have not voted vote red, the putting down (script 4), and with two white lamps the good lift's script ($15FF)

held too long: every judge left votes red, then one of two endings, script 6 when a random number is at least $4F and script 5 when it is below; a lift with two white lamps already given still counts. $4F comes from the first letter of the text "CURRENT WEIGHT" ($16F5, the C, $43, times 5), read here as if it were a number
the lifter's colour (sprite 1) as the hold goes on, a step every 64 frames: light red, orange, red, purple, blue
one judge's vote: a random judge of the three who has not voted ($15AB) gets the white lamp, counted in $46, while the hold is under 48 frames, or else the red one
where each judge's pair of lamps is in colour RAM, from $DAD3: 0, 16 and 31; the white lamp first, the red two cells on
every judge who has not voted (the white lamp still grey, colour 12) gets the red lamp
waits until the running script has ended ($3A bit 6)
the fire button of the lifter's joystick ($43, read by the interrupt): carry set once for each press, with six frames ($42) before another counts
waits for the script to end; with two white lamps or more, the good lift's celebration (script 7)
the powers of two from 1 to 8192 in binary-coded decimal, two bytes each, for $14B2
the high bytes of the same, read as $1616,X
"SNATCH #n" or "CLEAN AND JERK #n" in text row 0, n the attempt ($39)
the event's texts, for $1D35: ASCII, the last character with bit 7 set. "   kg" first, its three spaces the weight's digits
the weight's tens digit, written by $1401
the weight's units digit, written by $140A
"Butch Badorsik (USA)", a name and country that nothing prints
"PRACTICE WHICH EVENT?", the practice's choice between the two lifts
eighteen spaces, a blank for text row 0
"   SNATCH #" and spaces; the attempt's digit at $16A7
the snatch's attempt digit, written by $1635
"    SNATCH    ", the practice's first choice
"CLEAN AND JERK #" and its attempt's digit, at $16CC
the clean and jerk's attempt digit, written by $1638
"CLEAN AND JERK", the practice's second choice
"PLEASE SELECT THE WEIGHT."
"CURRENT WEIGHT "; its first byte is also read by $1549 as a number
"PRESS THE BUTTON TO START.", "PRESS THE BUTTON TO CONTINUE." from $171E, "BEGIN LIFT." from $173B, "PRACTICE AGAIN? " from $1746, "YES" and "NO "
the joystick of the current player: on the first attempt of the snatch, the port the player has just moved (X) is kept for the player in $1779; later it is taken from there. Into $53
the joystick port of each of the eight players, learned on the first snatch

the interrupt, through $FFFE: a BRK goes on to the KERNAL's vector at $0316; otherwise CIA 1's interrupt is acknowledged and a raster interrupt goes to the handler whose address is in the JMP at $1798, one of three in turn
the JMP's operand, the next raster handler: $17F2 at line 160, $17A4 at line 224, $17C7 at line 0
the high byte of the next handler's address
the registers back and the return from the interrupt
line 224: waits for line 226 and switches multicolour off ($D016 = $C8), so the three text rows at the bottom are drawn in hires; the next interrupt at line 0
line 0: when the event is over ($55) blanks the screen and goes to the shell's restart ($0900); otherwise multicolour on again, the next interrupt at line 160, and the frame counter $3B

line 160, the frame's work, with interrupts allowed again: the lifter's joystick into $43 (until it is known, $53 negative, whichever port is held for six frames becomes it, $175C); then, unless the script has ended, its next step ($183D); the plates redrawn if the weight has changed; a frame of music ($2803) and the fire button's wait ($42)

the lift's timing window, while one is open ($2B frames left): a push of the window's direction counts the timing (the frames left over the size of the good part, $2D, times 128, $1DF2) into $26-$27 and the number of pushes into $40, then the script goes on at $12-$13 if the push came in the good part, the last $2D frames, or at $14-$15 if it came too early. Then the pose's frames ($2A) count down, and at 0 the next step

the script's commands, from ($10): 0 and a byte ends the script with that result ($3D, $3A bit 6); $F0 and an address calls a part of the script, $F3 returns from it; $F4 and an address is where a push too early goes; $F6 and a byte starts that tune; another $F1-$FF opens a timing window: its low four bits are the joystick's directions, then its length in frames and where a good push goes. A byte below $F0 is a pose's length in frames, followed by the pose ($1930)
a pose: its frames in $2A and its number in $F0, its sprites' shapes copied ($1E3A) and placed ($1E8B); the first pose shown while $3A bit 7 is set ends the script there
the plates redrawn ($1A14) until they are at the weight
starts script A from the list at $2000, its first step at the next frame
the next of the 256 random bytes at $0400

the plates for the weight in $38: the weight less 25 kg in steps of 5, from which a plate for each 100 kg ($E0 bit 7) and each 50 kg ($E0 bit 6) is taken, and the rest gives the size and place of the last plate ($E1-$E4) and the bar ends' pixel patterns ($E5, $E6)
the pixel patterns of the bar's ends for the number of big plates: left-hand bytes
the right-hand bytes

draws the plates into the bitmap on both sides of the lifter, at the height the pose gives ($2700): the old ones wiped first ($1BB6), then the bar's stubs and each plate, a vertical strip of bytes at a time ($1C31, $1C50), the big ones as tall strips, the last one by its size; $2E keeps the weight drawn
wipes the plates drawn at the height kept in $F2, and puts the bar ends' bytes back

sets up a vertical strip for the column writer: its entry ($18-$19), three bytes on for each pixel line down ($30), and an RTS written at the line where it ends ($31 lines on); $32 keeps where, so the STA can be put back ($9D)
writes A down the strip at column offset X, through the entry at $18-$19
a straight run of 75 STA instructions, one for each pixel line down the plates' column of the bitmap; $1C31 starts it at a line and ends it with an RTS
prints the text at ($1A) in text row X (0-2, the bitmap's character rows 22 to 24) from column Y: each character's eight bytes from the font at $3800, the last character marked by bit 7
the low byte of the character's address in the font, worked out here
the high byte of the character's address: $07 shifted with the character, so the font starts at $3800
clears text row X: the 320 bytes of the bitmap at its address from $1DC5
the operand of the first clearing loop's STA, set to the row's address
its high byte
the operand of the second clearing loop's STA, the row's last 64 bytes
its high byte, one more than the row's
the bitmap address of each text row: $7B80, $7CC0, $7E00 (character rows 22, 23 and 24)
the high bytes, read as $1DC6,X
A times $24 (the window's length): the high byte of the product, in A and $23

divides $1E-$1F by A times 256; the quotient, scaled by 128, in $22-$23 and the high byte in A. The judges' delay ($14F9) takes that high byte of the average of the pushes' timing; each push's timing is below 128, so the high byte, and the delay, are always 0 and the first judge votes at once
copies the pose's sprite shapes to the VIC's bank at $F7-$F8 ($4000): its entry in the list at $8100 gives the number of sprites, then for each its place and the address of its 64 bytes
the copy's source, the shape's address, written for each sprite
the high byte of the shape's address, written for each sprite
the copy's destination, 64 bytes further for each sprite
the high byte of the copy's destination
the operand of CPY: four times the number of sprites, written here

places the pose's sprites: X and Y from the pose plus the event's origin ($FA, $F9), the shapes' pointers in the screen's last bytes ($5FF8), and from each shape's own 64th byte its colour (low nibble), multicolour (bit 7), double width (bit 6) and double height (bit 5)
the operand of CPX: two times the number of sprites, written here
the operand of the read of each shape's 64th byte, written for each sprite
the high byte of the address of the shape's 64th byte
the operand of CPX: the number of sprites, written here
the eight sprites' bits, 1 to 128
207 bytes of 0 that nothing reads, to the end of $1FFF

where each of the lift's eight scripts starts: 0 the lifter standing, 1 where script 0's windows go, 2 the snatch, 3 the clean and jerk, 4 putting the weight down, 5 and 6 the endings after holding too long, 7 the good lift
the high byte of script 0's address, read with the low byte as $2001,Y
the scripts' steps, read by $1894: poses with their lengths, the timing windows, calls and tunes; $2010-$21B1, then 0 to $23FF
for each of the 97 poses, the height of the bar in the column writer's lines, less 4: $40 with the bar on the floor, smaller as it rises
the bar heights, the last of the 97 poses, then 0 to $27FF
the music's jump table: start tune A ($280C)
the jump table's second entry: play a frame ($2889)
the jump table's third entry: build the frequency table ($283A)
the jump table's fourth entry: silence ($2872)

starts tune A: for each voice, the track the tune gives it ($2CFF, from four times A less two), its data pointer ($90-$95) and a wait of one tick ($B1-$B3); a voice whose entry is $FF is left as it is. The processor's interrupt flag is kept
builds the frequency table at $3700: eight octaves of twelve notes, each octave the top one ($2CDE) shifted right, note n at $3700 + 2n; falls into the silence
silences the music: clears the SID's registers and the driver's variables ($90-$D1), the pulse sweep's start at $0400 and the tempo at one frame a tick ($CF, $D0)

plays one frame of music: every $CF frames a tick ($D0 counts), in which each voice whose note has run out reads its next commands and note; one frame before the tick, the gates of the notes that are not held are let go. Every frame, the pulse width sweep ($BC) and the vibrato ($C2)
reads the voice's next byte: $EA is skipped, $FF ends the voice (pointer cleared, gate off), below $C0 a note ($2C26), otherwise a command from the table at $2C94
the next voice
the pulse width sweep for the voices that have it ($BC), up and down between $0200 and $0E00 by $0F a frame, or $10 when the carry is left set

the vibrato: every voice in $C2 counts its period down ($C9) and turns its direction round (bit 7 of $C4) when it runs out, adding or subtracting the step to its frequency; then the three frequencies are written to the SID
the offset of each voice's registers from $D400: 0, 7 and 14
command $C1: the voice's frequency, two bytes, straight to the SID
command $DD: a pulse wave ($40) with the pulse width at $0800
command $C2: the voice's waveform (its control register without the gate), one byte
command $C3: the voice's pulse width, two bytes
command $C4: the voice's envelope, attack-decay then sustain-release
command $C5: the filter's cutoff, low then high byte
command $C9: lowers the filter's cutoff by a byte, then reads a length as a note does
command $D6: raises the filter's cutoff by a byte, then a length
command $C6: the filter's resonance, the high nibble of a byte
command $C0: adds a byte to the volume, the result kept below 16
command $C7: the volume, the low nibble of a byte, with the filter type kept
command $C8: a wait: the voice reads nothing more for that many ticks
command $CA: puts the voice through the filter
command $CB: the filter type, the high nibble of a byte, with the volume kept
command $CC: takes the voice out of the filter
command $CD: sets the voice's first repeat count ($A7)
command $CE: a repeat: two bytes, an address the voice goes back to until the first repeat count runs out
command $D1: sets the voice's second repeat count ($A4)
command $D2: the second repeat, as $CE with the count at $A4
command $DA: lowers the frequency's high byte by a byte, then a length
command $CF: lowers the frequency by a byte, then a length
command $D9: raises the frequency's high byte by a byte, then a length
command $D0: raises the frequency by a byte, then a length
command $DB: vibrato on for the voice: its step and direction ($C4), then its period ($C3, $C9)
command $DC: vibrato off for the voice
command $D3: pulse width sweep on for the voice
command $D4: pulse width sweep off for the voice
each voice's bit, 1, 2 and 4, for the driver's masks of voices
each voice's bit cleared, $FE, $FD and $FB
command $D7: detune on for the voice: a byte the note's frequency is lowered by
command $D8: detune off
command $D5: a random note, number 31 to 95, which the SID's voice 3 output ($D41B) picks
command $DE: sets $CC to $FF, lets the gate go, and ends the voice's reading for the tick
command $DF: sets the voice's bit in $CD and stores a byte in $CE
command $E0: clears the voice's bit in $CD
command $E1: the gate on again, with the voice's waveform, and on to the next byte
command $E4: the tempo slower by a byte, the frames a tick added to
command $E3: the tempo faster by a byte
command $E2: the tempo, the frames a tick ($CF), one byte

a note: two times its number indexes the frequency table at $3700; the rest note, $60, only lets the gate go. The frequency goes to the SID, lowered by the voice's detune if it has it; the gate on. Then its length ($2C6E): bit 7 holds the gate, bits 0-6 are the ticks
the note's length: bit 7 holds the gate when the length runs out, bits 0-6 are the ticks
